feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete scope indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M page views, 50+ publishers). It reads clearly and professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with overlapping skills sections and a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in director and consultant roles, which strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Good use of scale and operational detail to show impact, especially in web modernization, analytics, and multimedia.  
- Strong positioning for public-sector digital leadership, with a consistent focus on governance, platforms, content operations, and AI-enabled experiences.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Tighten wording and add more outcome-focused metrics where possible; several bullets describe responsibilities more than results.  
- Fix style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler; title case and punctuation vary slightly across sections. No major misspellings found, but maintain consistency in hyphenation (e.g., “front-end,” “member-facing,” “public-facing”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground the most relevant differentiators: public-sector scale, platform modernization, governance, and analytics.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language such as “leading” or “delivering” to sound more executive.
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Builds scalable editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve discovery, coordination, and digital performance.”
- Standardize style: use either “AI-enabled” consistently everywhere and consider “public sector” vs. “public-sector” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The list of functions mirrors Core Competencies closely; avoid repeating the same capability stack in both places.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad digital functions.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Prioritize the most senior, differentiating strengths first: governance, platform modernization, analytics, AI search, and workflow integration.
- Replace broader items with sharper terms: “Multi-channel communications operations” → “Cross-channel communications operations”; “Advocacy and public-sector communications” → “Public-sector advocacy communications.”
- Suggested version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Cross-channel communications operations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Consider trimming overlap with the header’s “enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences.”
- Several items also repeat Topline Skills categories almost verbatim.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats several themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp line with parallel structure.
- Replace generic verbs (“Built,” “Developed”) with more differentiated ones and add outcomes where possible (e.g., improved discovery, supported campaign growth, expanded advocacy reach).
- Standardize style: use either sentence fragments or full sentences throughout; spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently.
- Consider this tighter version: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery. We Are Counties Microsite — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and modular architecture for future expansion…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with NACo roles in Work Experience.
- “Editorial storytelling” and “production/distribution across website, email and social” repeat themes already covered elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list rather than a high-impact recent position. Tighten around 3–4 highest-value contributions and add outcomes, scope, or named initiatives where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Improved cross-channel communications operations by refining workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make technical/build work more outcome-led: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits to support advocacy and engagement campaigns.”
- Add measurable scope/results if available: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, user adoption, search improvement, publishing efficiency, or troubleshooting turnaround.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording overlaps with prior NACo roles on governance, analytics, and digital operations; emphasize consultant-level advisory/build work rather than repeating team leadership themes.
- The AI search and microsite work also appears in Recent Projects, so keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Combine the website bullets and keep the strongest numbers: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-oriented; add performance if available (open rates, follower growth, engagement, production volume). Replace “serving thousands of followers” with a stronger metric or cut it.
- Tighten the remaining bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” / “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery reporting…” / “Established governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-programming language overlaps with both the footer projects and earlier NACo roles.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, repeatable systems, and channel growth.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: newsletter ownership, launch/growth of recurring advocacy video, cross-team editorial planning, and workflow standardization.
- Replace soft phrasing like “helped improve” and “helping establish” with direct ownership: “standardized,” “launched,” “expanded,” “institutionalized.”
- Add metrics if available: email open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this version tactical and execution-focused.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership capabilities not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Make governance more operational and distinctive: “Editorial systems and governance” → “Editorial governance, publishing standards, and cross-team content operations.”
- Refine “Multi-channel communications leadership” to stress scale and coordination: “Integrated web, email, social, and video communications leadership.”
- Swap “Audience-focused content planning” for a stronger planning/decision lens: “Audience and analytics-informed content strategy.”

Possible rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Integrated web, email, social, and video leadership
- Advocacy and public-sector communications
- Audience- and analytics-informed content strategy

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep one phrasing only.
- “Editorial systems and governance” is very close to “Digital governance & editorial systems” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize recent strengths tied to Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing; lead with strongest, most recent areas.
- Cut lower-priority or older-signal items unless they are job-target critical.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- Airtable-based operational systems
- AI-enabled search and content discovery
- WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages
- If space allows, replace one platform name with a stronger outcome-oriented phrase like “modular microsite builds” or “large-scale content migrations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost verbatim; keep this version higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “CMS modernization” and “Drupal” are both strong, but avoid repeating every platform in multiple sections.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” rather than all as separate bullets.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger wording: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity - KPI framework development and executive dashboarding - SEO, user behavior and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Performance analysis” may overlap with broader “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo multimedia bullets. Make it more senior, outcomes-oriented, and tied to recent leadership-level delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- In-house studio buildout and operations  
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows  
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. “supporting advocacy programming and recurring organizational broadcasts.”
- Keep phrasing parallel and avoid listing tools here unless they signal scope; detailed software already appears in Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” duplicate Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”).
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so this section should stay concise rather than repeat job-detail language.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a recent senior digital leader, this item should signal depth and modernization relevance, not just name tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize level and use case: “Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Put strongest/recent platform first and consider dropping weaker/less strategic tools if space is tight; Drupal is clearly the anchor based on recent roles.
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of more platforms: “Drupal 10,” “enterprise publishing,” or “multi-publisher environments.”
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” rather than “Power Pages.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution”; consider merging or making one broader and this one more specific.
- GitHub Pages may undersell your seniority unless tied to a clear use case or removed.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, emphasize implementation strengths that support recent Drupal, analytics, AI/search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more specific, e.g. **Front-End & Technical Implementation** or **Development & Integration Tools**.
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, REST/API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**.
- If accurate, group by function for readability: **Front-end:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery | **Integration & deployment:** API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions | **Tagging:** Google Tag Manager.
- If space allows, add one brief qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “used for Drupal front-end implementation, analytics tagging, and lightweight workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed in Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap conceptually with analytics infrastructure elsewhere; keep here only if this section is tool-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and keep only strongest, most relevant tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Drop lower-value/general tools unless heavily used in recent roles: Basecamp, Trello
- Standardize naming for professionalism: “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams”
- If accurate, add a light proficiency cue in the heading or formatting, e.g., “Automation & Workflow Systems (advanced)” or order by depth/recent use

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same emphasis elsewhere unless this section is trimmed to tools only
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are project-management tools; too many similar platforms can dilute the stronger automation message

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the scale/ownership already shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations and member engagement, not just tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize phrasing: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add light context to show level of use: **Enterprise email campaign operations, newsletter distribution, audience segmentation and engagement workflows**
- Consider moving the strongest platform first based on most recent use; if NACo primarily used Higher Logic, list that first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Work Experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; keep this item tool-focused and avoid repeating audience-size claims here.
- “Engagement” is broad and may blur with analytics/communications leadership elsewhere unless tied specifically to email/member platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the Director role. Make it more capability-led and slightly sharper on business use.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • SEO analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing)**
- Replace “Dashboarding” with **KPI design** or **executive reporting**; “dashboarding” is vague and implied by Looker Studio/Power BI.
- Consider changing “SEO” to **SEO analysis** or **search performance analysis** to sound more specific and senior.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to outcomes in recent roles rather than listing them here alone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly a duplicate of **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one version or making this one tools-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available outputs or audience metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Tighten and specify contributions: website refresh, livestream/event production, weekly video series, and cross-channel publishing workflows.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/events produced, video cadence, email/social volume supported, or size of team/process improvements.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved publishing workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Also provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early production support.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; make this entry more tactical and execution-oriented.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a clear throughline into later digital/media leadership, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia work. Emphasize the podcast launch as the standout achievement and tighten the rest around scope and purpose.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the most distinctive outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and strongest proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer contribution such as “supported digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one metric or scope detail: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of research/projects coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia production, which is covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t repeat “first” team-building language from the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on research coordination + podcast launch.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Tighten it to software/tools only, and use stronger, more current phrasing tied to professional production.
